newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain balance unaffected by floods-minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain balance unaffected by floods-minister.

text.p: Poland's overall grain balance will not be affected by the past week's heavy flooding because of the country's large reserves, but farms in some regions have been hit hard, agriculture minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski said on Monday.

"Our grain reserves in Poland are considerable. There is no danger that this may influence our balance of grain in any way, but for those (affected) regions the situation will be very hard," he told public radio.
The government's Agriculture Market Agency (ARR) would draw on reserves to provide affected farmers with what they needed to resume production, Kalinowski said.

Kalinowski said 400,000 hectares of Poland were flooded and, after adding areas that had been under water, the total area affected by the bad weather was 600,000 ha. While much of this was pasture, there was also grain and other crops.
"It is hard for me to say what the losses are, but they are enormous," Kalinowski said, adding that in the southwestern region of Opole, for example, 80 percent of livestock had died.

Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said estimates of damage to crops would take until mid-August to produce. She said Poland would not have to import additional food because of its large reserves.
